opportunities.title: Early Career Fellowships

amount.raw: Fellowships can be held at UK universities with research degree awarding powers. The Fellowships are intended to assist those at a relatively early stage of their academic careers, and it is hoped that the appointment would lead to a more permanent position for the individual, either within the same or another university.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: For early career researchers, with a research record but who have not yet held a full-time permanent academic post, to undertake a significant piece of publishable work.

opportunities.title: Art Scholarship Training Opportunities Under 18s

amount.raw: Each institution can apply for a maximum total award of £475,000.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: For specialist arts institutions or registered charities to provide training opportunities across the fine and performing arts for school-age children under 18 outside of regular school hours, e.g. for weekends or evenings or during holiday periods.

opportunities.opportunity_id: Art Scholarship Bursaries for Undergraduates and Postgraduates
opportunities.title: Art Scholarship Bursaries for Undergraduates and Postgraduates

amount.raw: Each institution can apply for a maximum total award of £475,000.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: For specialist arts institutions or registered charities to provide support to undergraduate and/or postgraduate students across the fine and performing arts, including music, drama, dance, film, fine art, etc.

opportunities.title: Emeritus Fellowships

amount.raw: Applications are invited for a minimum value of £3,000 and a maximum of £24,000.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: For senior researchers who have retired or partially retired from an academic post to complete a research project and prepare the results for publication.

opportunities.title: Leverhulme Centenary Doctoral Scholarships

amount.raw: Up to £5 million is available for up to 30 Leverhulme Centenary Doctoral Scholarships at UK/home rates and 6 four-year Scholarships at international/overseas rates.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: For UK universities to fund up to 30 Leverhulme Centenary Doctoral Scholarships in an interdisciplinary priority research area for that institution.

opportunities.title: Leverhulme Research Centres

amount.raw: Up to £10 million is available for up to 10 years.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: For UK universities to set up a Leverhulme Research Centre for outstanding original research aspiring to achieve a step-change in scholarship.

opportunities.title: Major Research Fellowships

amount.raw: The maximum value of a Fellowship is £70,000.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: For experienced researchers to complete a piece of research.

opportunities.title: Philip Leverhulme Prizes
opportunities.eligibility_summary: For well-established, distinguished researchers in the humanities and social sciences to complete a piece of original research.

opportunities.title: Research Fellowships

amount.raw: The maximum value of a Fellowship is £70,000.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: For experienced researchers to complete a piece of research.

opportunities.title: Research Leadership Awards

amount.raw: Each award will be for up to £1 million, for staff salaries and associated costs.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: For talented scholars who are embarking on a university career who need to build a research team of sufficient scale to tackle a distinctive research problem.

opportunities.title: Research Project Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: For researchers based at universities or institutions of higher education, to undertake an innovative and original research project.

opportunities.title: Visiting Professorships

amount.raw: Applications are invited for a minimum of £10,000 and a maximum of £150,000.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: For UK institutions to invite an eminent senior professor from overseas, to bring genuinely novel expertise and enhance the skills and knowledge of academic staff and students in an underrepresented area of research, within the UK.
